item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
It's pretty dependent on how interested you are in the fate of the people who die near it. If you're only concerned about locking things up and keeping them locked up, this object isn't going to thrill you.
But if you're curious about the implications of the effect, whether the "souls" go to the heaven, or a fake subjective heaven, or if they're devoured/assimilated… well then it starts to get a bit mysterious.

If you owned this dog, would you take it with you into a war zone?
Your friend just got his head taken off by enemy fire. You took a hit and you're not going to make it. But a big, friendly, fuzzy companion is comforting you and taking the pain away. And your friend's voice is there to comfort you and let you know it'll be alright. That there's something better waiting for you and you don't have to fight anymore.
OR
Are you just being lured into the gaping maw of Cerberus himself, who has enslaved the very souls of people he consumes?

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
That's why I said this is such a great SCP. It's a simple concept, but done in a way that leads to a great deal of discussion possibilties.

From a psychological standpoint, this dog could be viewed as the personification of death. It could be evil, it could be good, it could just be a thing that happens, or it could be that this thing is just a remarkable coincidence. The point is: we don't know.

It took me a while to understand that, but that's why I like this SCP so much. It makes you think.

item.content:encoded:
That's what I assumed. The dog itself just suppresses pain, without even knowing that it's doing so. It has no idea that these strange disembodied voices are using it to make people kill themselves.

My personal take on 916 is that originally, he was just a dog who happened to be born with empathic pain-suppressing powers. (In a world where other animals have spontaneously become sapient and humans have developed reality-warping powers, it's not that hard to believe.) Then someone suicidal took advantage of the dog's pain-suppressing powers to kill himself. Because he took the easy way out, his spirit became trapped as a ghost, and now he's using the dog's powers to get other people to join him. He might also be responsible for the dog's immortality, or that might just be a part of the dog's natural mutation.

item.content:encoded:
In a lot of SCPs, there's an initial suspense built up by the bizarre containment procedure. It precedes the description, so I'm increasingly curious what the hell we're talking about.

In a few SCPs, it's almost the opposite. The containment procedure makes it seem perfectly obvious what is being contained, and I have to wonder, what is the catch? It can't be that simple, can it? And eventually, somewhere in the description, it suddenly gets strange.

This is a good example of the latter. That's just a picture of a friendly dog. This containment procedure… it's just a dog. What's going on? Is it just a dog? A very long-lived dog? Well, okay, but that's hardly even… wait, what?

Oh, and I thought of Oscar, too. Actually, when I first read of Oscar, I wasn't sure whether to think it was charming or disturbing, and that's what I got with this story.

I actually agree, I think part of what makes this article work for me isn't the grizzly "bite your tongue and bleed out" bit, it's more the "dying painlessly" bit. I can imagine this dog wandering around nursing homes and hospitals, going to the people who are in severe pain and easing them into a painless, comfortable death.

This article is neat because for me it has two interpretations: either the voice is telling the truth about the afterlife and really does just want to help ailing souls find peace (but for whatever reason doesn't know how to differentiate between "ailing" and "totally fine"), or the voice is lying and their death actually does something horrible, like feeding Satan or something. The hopeful in me leans towards the former, while the cynic in me leans towards the latter.

Either way, the Foundation has now contained the Angel of Death.

And it's a dog.
